title: India call-bridge: the agent's own phone rings first, then the customer (provider per G1 addendum)
goal: Let Indian agencies call customers through the platform by ringing the agent's mobile and then the customer, which fits India's rules.
why: ADR-001: India launches with call-bridge only (both legs on the Indian phone network) pending legal confirmation; the owner could not sign up with Plivo (2026-10-14) and the ADR addendum will name the India provider; nothing implements the bridge.
steps: Each agent stores a verified mobile number (profile; verified by a login-code style check from R110).

Outbound in bridge mode: placeCall({ mode: bridge, agentNumber, to }) rings the agent first, plays a short whisper ("Connecting you to <contact>"), then dials the customer with the agency's Indian number as caller ID; events and recording as in R302/R303/R306.
Inbound in bridge mode: the routed agent's mobile rings (no softphone); the desktop screen pop appears at the same time (R303).
Country policy (R304) decides bridge for IN; a not-yet-confirmed softphone in India stays hidden.
tests: backend/test/call-bridge.test.ts: outbound bridge places the agent leg first then the customer leg (mock provider order); unverified agent mobile -> 409; inbound bridge dials the agent mobile; metering counts both legs per the provider records.
acceptance: Bridge flows pass with the mock provider (tests).
gate: cd backend && npx vitest run   # pass: 0 failed files and passed >= the last merged count (1296 on 2026-10-14)
cd desktop && npx tsc --noEmit && npx tsc -p electron/tsconfig.json --noEmit
cd desktop && npx vitest run   # pass: 0 failing files, passed >= last merged count (1294 on 2026-10-14)
goLiveVerify: An Indian provider account per the ADR-001 addendum (Twilio has no domestic Indian calling), KYC, written confirmation on sub-accounts, telecom lawyer opinion (ADR 9a items 2, 3, 10).
notes: Before editing read: this batch file, docs/readiness/READINESS-PLAN.md sections 0 and the design note for this area, desktop/audit/fix/FIX-PLAN.md sections 3-4 (executor rules, worktree bootstrap with node_modules junctions; never npm install inside a worktree unless the batch adds a dependency, and then only in the main checkout by the orchestrator).

Backend tests follow the existing pattern (see backend/test/voip-callbacks.test.ts): import env, createExecutionContext, waitOnExecutionContext, applyD1Migrations from cloudflare:test; applyD1Migrations(env.MASTER_DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS) in beforeAll; POST /api/v1/test/reset; call worker.fetch(request, env, ctx). isolatedStorage is false and singleWorker true, so use unique ids/emails per test file.

Read docs/decisions/ADR-001-voip.md (sections 4, 6, 7), its addendum when it exists (the owner could not sign up with Plivo; the addendum settles the default provider, likely Twilio where it can serve, with India handled separately), and docs/CALL-AUTOMATION.md (sections 2, 3, 4). Everything here stays behind the VoipProvider interface; do not design around Plivo. Calls are included in plans with a monthly minute cap (owner decision 2026-10-14).
Blocked on G1: the ADR-001 addendum (provider) must be signed first.
